```dockerfile
FROM node:22-alpine AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts

FROM node:22-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:22-alpine AS runner
ENV NODE_ENV=production
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts && npm cache clean --force
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```

Three stages and why each matters:

**`deps`** — installs all dependencies (including devDependencies) in isolation. Cached independently so a source-only change doesn't re-run `npm ci`.

**`builder`** — copies source and compiled output (`dist/`) using the full dep tree. Nothing from this stage bleeds into the final image.

**`runner`** — starts clean, installs only production deps (`--omit=dev`), copies only `dist/`. No TypeScript compiler, no source files, no devDependencies.

A few things to adjust for your project:

- Change `dist/index.js` to match your `outDir` + entrypoint in `tsconfig.json`
- If your `npm run build` calls `tsc` with a project flag, it will just work — no changes needed
- `--ignore-scripts` skips lifecycle scripts (e.g. `postinstall`) for security; remove it if you have a required `postinstall` step
- Add a `.dockerignore` to keep the build context lean:

```
node_modules
dist
.git
*.md
```
